authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: No redundant low-impact lifegain artifacts from EDHREC (L35).

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Enchantment or creature removal on loop pieces; the deck needs both halves.
Sol'kanar alone is slow incremental value.
Too few blue cards to pitch to Force of Will.

value.interaction: Counterspell, Mana Drain, Swan Song, Fierce Guardianship, Withering Torment, Deadly Rollick, Toxic Deluge, Cyclonic Rift.
value.mana: 36 land-capable slots (Swamp-typed duals, Coffers) plus Mox Diamond, Chrome Mox and Lotus Petal.

cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

accepted_role.advances_plan: Sol'kanar gains 1 life per black spell, which starts the life loops, and has swampwalk once Blanket of Night or Urborg is out.
accepted_role.honest_note: Honest call: supporting. None of the 13 Spellbook combos uses Sol'kanar; the loops start from any lifegain, and Demon's Horn duplicates the trigger. The source itself calls him a five-mana incremental trigger engine (blueprint L26). The deck is a strong two-card life-loop deck built around a modest commander. M1 review (solkanar-01..06, all verified) confirms the trigger and loop rules.
